lines.text: The arcade kid laughed at my grandpa... worst mistake of his life.

lines.text: For my birthday, Grandpa took me to the new retro arcade. He's seventy-four.

image.prompt: {grandpa} and {ollie} walking through the entrance of a colorful retro arcade full of glowing cabinets, neon purple and blue lights, Ollie excited, Grandpa calm and smiling, wide shot

lines.text: He walked right past everything... straight to one dusty old machine in the corner.

image.prompt: {grandpa} standing still in front of a dusty old arcade cabinet in a dark corner, staring at it like he knows it, soft blue screen glow

lines.text: The worker, Chad, laughed. 'Sir, that one's for real gamers.'

lines.text: They bought it from an old arcade that closed. Its top score hadn't been beaten since 1986.

image.prompt: {chad} with arms crossed bragging next to a glowing old arcade cabinet, smug face, {ollie} listening, neon lights

lines.text: A legend nobody ever met. Just three letters... T. J. R.

lines.text: Grandpa held out one quarter and said... 'One game.'

lines.text: Ten minutes later, a crowd was watching.

lines.text: Forty minutes later, Chad wasn't laughing anymore.

lines.text: One quarter. New record. And then Grandpa typed in three letters... T. J. R.

lines.text: Grandpa's name is Thomas James Reed. That record was his.

lines.text: He quit in '86. Grandma said it was her or the machine... and he picked her.

lines.text: Now Chad gives him free quarters every Saturday. Because the last time...
